title: Engineering MoO 3 /AgO@rGO heterostructure for enhanced supercapacitive energy storage and bifunctional water splitting
content: The development of multifunctional electrode materials capable of combining efficient energy storage with electrocatalytic water splitting is highly desirable for sustainable energy technologies. In this work, a novel MoO3/AgO@rGO trifunctional nanoheterostructure was fabricated through a simple ultrasonic-assisted mixing route for supercapacitor, hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), and oxygen evolution reaction (OER) applications. The structural, surface, and morphological characteristics of the synthesized materials were investigated using XRD, XPS, SEM, and BET analyses. The incorporation of MoO3 and AgO with wrinkled rGO sheets produced an interconnected porous architecture with a specific surface area of approximately 89.6 m2 g−1 and an average pore diameter of about 3.5 nm. As a supercapacitor electrode, the MoO3/AgO@rGO achieved a specific capacitance of 453.33 F g−1 at 2 A g−1, an energy density (Ed) of 12.8 Wh kg−1, and a power density (Pd) of 1144.79 W kg−1 while retaining 94.5% of its initial capacitance after 6000 cycles. The MoO3/AgO@rGO nanoheterostructure exhibited OER overpotential of 280 mV and a Tafel slope of 52 mV dec−1 at 10 mA cm−2, whereas the HER overpotential was 323 mV with a Tafel slope of 154 mV dec−1. Its high electrochemically accessible surface area and quick reaction kinetics are further demonstrated by a double-layer capacitance of 41.5 mF cm−2 and charge-transfer resistance of 83 Ω. These results establish MoO3/AgO@rGO as a feasible integrated platform for next-generation electrochemical energy conversion and storage.
